clue.text: Talk of child's dog having new lead

indicators.note: a fresh lead means the first letter of the dog word is swapped for another

parts.note: bow-wow is a nursery word for a dog

explanation.surface: A remark about a youngster's pet getting a new leash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having new lead' swaps the B at the front of BOWWOW for P; the lead in the surface is a dog lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A powwow is an informal meeting or discussion, hence a talk.

clue.text: What one did after acquiring euros in part of Paris?

definitions.text: What one did after acquiring euros
definitions.meaning: having withdrawn cash, you walked out of the financial institution
the southern side of the Seine, the Rive Gauche

explanation.surface: A riddle about what someone did once they had their euros in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rive Gauche, south of the Seine, is the famous artistic district known in English by this name.

clue.text: Top vet nursed bull

indicators.note: bull is nonsense, so the letters before it are rearranged into new order

explanation.surface: A vet at the top of the profession tended a bull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bull' (nonsense) signals the anagram of VET NURSED; 'Top' is a garment, not 'best'.
explanation.definitionFit: An undervest is a garment worn on the upper body, a kind of top.

clue.text: Boy, first in every test, has academic nous

indicators.note: first in applies to each of the following words, taking its opening letter

explanation.surface: A clever boy came top in every exam because he has academic intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'first in every test' reads as coming top; really 'first in' takes the initials of the five words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethan is a boy's given name.

clue.text: Knock drink back during work, as expected

indicators.note: during places the reversed piece within the word for work

parts.note: to ply is to work at a trade

indicators.note: back tells us knock and drink are read in reverse order and spelling

parts.note: to bat is to hit or knock
cider is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Someone downs a drink at work, as you might expect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses knock-plus-drink as one run, giving REDICTAB, and 'during' sets that inside the word for work; 'Knock' here means hit, not criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: Predictably means in a way that could be foreseen, i.e. as one would anticipate.

clue.text: Whistler's Mother, effective to an extent

indicators.note: only partly present, so the letters lie within the words mother effective

explanation.surface: Whistler's famous painting of his mother, described as effective in part.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous painting 'Whistler's Mother' misleads: the whistler is a referee, and 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A football referee blows the whistle, so a whistler is a referee, shortened to its familiar form.

clue.text: Computer technology accepted by great writer

indicators.note: accepted by puts the computing abbreviation inside the word for great

parts.note: swell is old slang for excellent or great
IT stands for information technology

explanation.surface: A great writer embraces computers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'great' looks like part of 'great writer' but supplies SWELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Sitwell was an English poet and critic, a celebrated literary figure.

clue.text: Recalls European film with very old content

indicators.note: content means held inside, so these abbreviations are contained in the other pieces

parts.note: Kes is a 1969 Ken Loach film about a boy and his kestrel

explanation.surface: A European film featuring very old material brings back memories.
explanation.walkthrough: KES is a classic British film about a boy and a kestrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke something is to bring it to mind, i.e. it recalls it.

clue.text: Back at university, scholar enters classes after vacation … here?

indicators.note: enters puts the reversed pieces inside the emptied classes
classes vacated keeps only its outer letters, the middle emptied
Back reads the university and scholar pieces in reverse

parts.note: up means at university, as in being up at Oxford
MA is a Master of Arts, a scholar

explanation.surface: After the holidays, a returning scholar goes back to classes at college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses the university and scholar pieces to give AMPU; 'after vacation' empties the classes; 'enters' sets one in the other. The whole clue also paints the place, a semi-&lit.
explanation.definitionFit: The campus is the grounds of a university, where students return to classes after a break.

clue.text: One performing piano work with brief introduction

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano
op. is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: brief means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: a start is an introduction or beginning

explanation.surface: A pianist playing a piece with a short introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' drops the last letter of START.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop star is a celebrity performer of popular music.

clue.text: Animal rescue transport heading away from island

indicators.note: the heading, or first letter, leaves the island's name

parts.note: Sark is one of the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: An animal-rescue vehicle leaving an island.
explanation.walkthrough: SARK is a small Channel Island; take off its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah's vessel saved the animals from the Flood.

clue.text: Vehicle, reverse of fleet, much criticised

indicators.note: reverse of reads both following pieces backwards together

parts.note: a navy is a nation's fleet
reviled means heavily criticised

explanation.surface: A vehicle, the opposite of a fleet, has been widely condemned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse of' turns the fleet and criticism words round as one run, giving DELIVERYVAN; read in the surface, 'reverse of' looks like 'the opposite of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A delivery van is a kind of vehicle used to carry goods.

clue.text: Poles distributed in ski area

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so the letters of poles are scattered

explanation.surface: Ski poles were handed out on the piste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like ski poles; it is just anagram material.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski slope is the run you ski down.

clue.text: Decrepit doctor ultimately banned from part of hospital during day

indicators.note: during places the trimmed hospital word inside the day abbreviation

parts.note: Mon is short for Monday

indicators.note: banned from removes the named letter from the hospital word

parts.note: an operating theatre is part of a hospital

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of doctor

explanation.surface: A frail doctor was finally barred from the operating room one day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' picks the last letter of doctor; 'banned from' removes it from the hospital word, leaving THEATE, which 'during' places inside the day. The surface's doctor is only a source of one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Moth-eaten means worn out and shabby, hence decrepit.

clue.text: Doctor No presented with award for variety? Not so

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
a Tony is a Broadway theatre award

explanation.surface: The Bond villain Doctor No receives a prize for a variety show.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor No is a Bond film villain, but here the two words give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Monotony is sameness and dullness, the opposite of variety.

clue.text: Old actress given makeover by Warhol

indicators.note: a makeover rearranges appearance, so the letters of Warhol are reordered

explanation.surface: A vintage film star restyled by Andy Warhol.
explanation.walkthrough: Warhol did make famous portraits of stars, which helps the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Harlow was a 1930s Hollywood film star.

clue.text: Fruit drink served up hot? Stout, rather

parts.note: a plum is a fruit

indicators.note: served up in a down clue reads the drink word upwards

parts.note: to sip is to drink

explanation.surface: Fruit punch served hot and a stout beer, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reverses SIP to PIS in this down clue; 'Stout' looks like the beer but means fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumpish means somewhat plump, i.e. fairly stout or chubby.

clue.text: Piece landing BBC boss in trouble

indicators.note: in places the boss abbreviation within the word for trouble

parts.note: woe means trouble or grief
the BBC is run by its Director General, DG

explanation.surface: An item putting the head of the BBC in hot water.
explanation.walkthrough: The BBC's chief executive is the Director General, DG.
explanation.definitionFit: A wodge is a large chunk or piece of something, a British informal word.

clue.text: One paddling round a river

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A paddler goes round a river.
explanation.definitionFit: An oar is a blade used by a rower, so it is something that paddles.

clue.text: Each thing available in restaurant should be

definitions.text: Each thing available in restaurant should be

parts.note: a restaurant offers tables to diners

explanation.surface: Every dish on a restaurant menu ought to be fit to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer while also supplying EA and TABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Food served in a restaurant ought to be fit for consumption.

clue.text: Two hats, Spooner might have said, for fashionable youngster?

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the starting sounds of words, so the initial sounds of the two hat words change places

parts.note: a beanie is a close-fitting knitted hat
a topper is a top hat

explanation.surface: Two hats suit a trendy young person.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the B and T sounds of BEANIE TOPPER gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenybopper is a young teenager who follows pop fashions.

clue.text: Horrible chore, expelling extremists in a London borough

indicators.note: in puts the trimmed chore inside the A and borough pieces

parts.note: Brent is a borough in north-west London

indicators.note: expelling the extremists drops the outer letters of chore

explanation.surface: A dreadful household chore that drives out radicals in a London borough.
explanation.walkthrough: BRENT is a north-west London borough; 'expelling extremists' leaves HOR from chore.
explanation.definitionFit: Abhorrent means detestable or repugnant, i.e. horrible.

clue.text: Self-defence needed, following wild beast in country to the north

indicators.note: to the north in a down clue means read upwards, reversing everything
in places the following-and-beast pieces within the country

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom
a gnu is a wildebeest

explanation.surface: Self-defence is needed after a wild animal appears up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sets following-plus-beast inside the country to make UFGNUK, and 'to the north' reads that upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Kung fu is a Chinese martial art used for self-defence.

clue.text: Intellectual displaying collection of books during dinner, perhaps

indicators.note: during places the books abbreviation within the meal

parts.note: dinner is an example of a meal
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A highbrow shows off his library at a dinner party.
explanation.walkthrough: The New Testament is a collection of books, abbreviated NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Mental means relating to the mind, as intellectual does.

clue.text: Undesirable in old gym wanting food about noon

parts.note: ex means former or old
PE is physical education, school gym

indicators.note: about puts the noon letter inside the food word

parts.note: a diet is the food a person eats

explanation.surface: It's unwise to skip lunch at an old gym.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexpedient means not advisable or not suitable, so undesirable.

clue.text: Find path from the summit?

definitions.meaning: a trail leading down a mountain

explanation.surface: Locating the way back down a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: To track down someone is to find them by searching; the phrase also describes a downhill trail.

clue.text: Fresh tea, with end of Bourbon dunked in

indicators.note: dunked in plunges the pieces into the tea word

parts.note: a brew is a pot or cup of tea
and means with, joining things

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of Bourbon

explanation.surface: A fresh cup of tea with a Bourbon biscuit dunked in it.
explanation.walkthrough: A Bourbon is a British chocolate sandwich biscuit, but only its last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Brand new means completely new and unused, i.e. fresh.

clue.text: Singer, male, performing, who was responsible for song?

parts.note: a solo is one voice singing alone
on means performing, as in on stage

explanation.surface: A male singer on stage, credited with writing the song.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'song' is the Song of Solomon (Song of Songs) in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical Song of Songs is traditionally attributed to King Solomon.

clue.text: Important people almost prevent bigwig getting rise

indicators.note: getting rise in a down clue reads the pieces upwards
almost means not quite complete, losing the last letter

parts.note: to stop is to prevent
a VIP is a very important person

explanation.surface: Most important people try to stop a bigwig getting a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts STOP to STO; STO VIP is then read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Pivots are key figures on whom things turn, so central people.

clue.text: Save crumbling manors

indicators.note: crumbling means falling apart, so the letters of manors are broken up

explanation.surface: Rescue the decaying country houses.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransom someone is to secure their release by payment, hence to rescue.

clue.text: Decisive victory initially over European country, except southernmost part

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of victory
in a down clue the southernmost part is the bottom letter, which is dropped

parts.note: Italy is a European country

explanation.surface: A decisive win over a European nation, apart from its far south.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'southernmost part' is the last letter, so ITALY loses its Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Vital means essential or crucial, so it can mean decisive.

clue.text: Greek character partner regularly upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the selection upside down
regularly takes every other letter of partner

explanation.surface: A Greek person's partner is often upset.
explanation.walkthrough: Even letters of partner give ATE, and 'upset' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet.
